accepted.question_text: Give a mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics, including an axiomatic treatment of probability with limit theorems suitable for the foundations of statistical physics and a rigorous theory of the limiting processes that connect atomistic descriptions to continuum laws of motion.

evidence.quote: • H6 Mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether every problem whose proposed solution can be verified in polynomial time can also be solved in polynomial time; equivalently, decide whether P = NP.

evidence.quote: • S3 Does P = NP?

accepted.question_text: Extend the mathematical model of general equilibrium theory so that it includes price adjustments rather than only equilibrium states.

evidence.quote: • S8 Extend the mathematical model of general equilibrium theory to include price adjustments.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the three-dimensional Navier–Stokes equations on R3 always admit a unique smooth solution that exists for all time.

evidence.quote: • S15 Do the Navier-Stokes equations in R3 always have a unique smooth solution that extends for all time?

accepted.question_text: Establish rigorously that quantum Yang–Mills theory exists and has a positive mass gap, meaning that although the classical field theory has massless gauge bosons, the quantum theory admits only massive bound states.

evidence.quote: • M2 Yang-Mills existence and mass gap.

accepted.question_text: For the Newtonian N-body problem of gravitating particles, prove that the set of initial conditions that fail to produce global solutions has measure zero, and determine whether non-collisional singularities can occur.

evidence.quote: • BS1 Existence for Newtonian Gravitating Particles. A: Prove that the set of initial conditions which fails to have global solutions is of measure zero ... B: Existence of non-collisional singularities in the Newtonian N-body problem.

accepted.question_text: Develop a comprehensive mathematical theory of the long-time behavior of dynamical systems that also explains the onset of turbulence and the regime of fully developed turbulence.

evidence.quote: • BS3 Develop a comprehensive theory of the long time behavior of dynamical systems including a theory of the onset of, and of fully developed, turbulence.

accepted.question_text: Resolve the open questions in ergodic theory highlighted here, including ergodicity of gases with soft cores, approach to equilibrium, and asymptotic Abelianness for quantum Heisenberg dynamics.

evidence.quote: • BS2 Open Questions in Ergodic Theory. Particular problems include A: Ergodicity of gases with soft cores, B: Approach to equilibrium, and C: Asymptotic Abelianness for the quantum Heisenberg dynamics.

accepted.question_text: Formulate a mathematically precise renormalization-group framework for Ising-type systems and prove universality, including the independence of critical exponents in three-dimensional nearest-neighbor Ising models from anisotropic bond-strength ratios.

evidence.quote: • BS8 Formulation of the Renormalization Group and Proof of Universality. A: Develop a mathematically precise version of the renormalization transformations for ν-dimensional Ising-type systems. B: In particular, show that the critical exponents in the three dimensional Ising models with nearest neighbor coupling but different bond strengths in the three directions are independent of the ratios of these bond strengths.

accepted.question_text: Clarify whether quantum field theory is mathematically consistent by carrying out the listed construction and inconsistency problems: give a precise construction of quantum chromodynamics, construct a nontrivial renormalizable but not super-renormalizable quantum field theory, prove that quantum electrodynamics is not a consistent theory, and prove that a nontrivial lattice cutoff theory does not exist.

evidence.quote: • BS14 Quantum field theory remains a basic element of fundamental physics ... A: give a precise mathematical construction of quantum chromodynamics ... B: Construct any non-trivial renormalizable but not super–renormalizable quantum field theory. C: Prove that quantum electrodynamics is not a consistent theory. D: Prove that a non-trivial lattice cutoff theories theory does not exist.

accepted.question_text: Prove that any Yang–Mills field on the 4-sphere S4 is either self-dual or anti-self-dual.

evidence.quote: • Y117 Prove that any YM field on S4 is either self-dual or antiself-dual.

accepted.question_text: Prove that the moduli space of self-dual fields on the 4-sphere S4 with a fixed Pontryagin number is connected.

evidence.quote: • Y118 Prove that the moduli space of the self-dual fields on S4 with a fixed Pontryagin number is connected.

accepted.question_text: Determine the range of validity of post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions used in general relativity.

evidence.quote: • RB20 Determine the range of validity of the post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions.

accepted.question_text: Prove rigorously that there is a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

evidence.quote: • RB21 Prove rigorously the existence of a limit in which solutions of the Einstein equations reduce to Newtonian spacetimes.

accepted.question_text: Prove that any cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R × M3 and is therefore static.

evidence.quote: • RB32 Prove that a “cosmological spacetime” satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete or it splits as R × M 3 isometrically (and is thus static).

accepted.question_text: Find an exact solution of the Einstein equations representing two orbiting bodies, and determine whether the two-body system is unstable in Einstein gravity.

evidence.quote: • RB43 Find an exact solution of the Einstein equations which represents two orbiting bodies. Is the 2-body system unstable in Einstein gravity?

accepted.question_text: Prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture, namely that generic gravitational collapse in general relativity does not produce naked singularities visible from infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem P1: Prove the weak cosmic censorship conjecture.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a 3-dimensional compact manifold. Prove that for generic vacuum initial data on M, the maximal vacuum Cauchy development equals the maximal vacuum extension of M.

evidence.quote: Problem P2: Let M be a 3 dimensional compact manifold. Prove that the maximal vacuum Cauchy development for generic vacuum data sets is equal to the maximal vacuum extension of M.

accepted.question_text: Either prove the Penrose inequality in full generality or produce a counterexample in the general case.

evidence.quote: Problem P3: Find a proof of the Penrose inequality or present a counterexample in the general case.

accepted.question_text: Prove global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data in collisionless matter models, and prove existence and uniqueness for general spatially homogeneous solutions of the Einstein–Vlasov equations while also investigating the large-initial-data regime.

evidence.quote: Problem P4 : Prove the global existence of classical spatially inhomogeneous solutions for small initial data in collisionless matter models. Prove an existence and uniqueness theorem for general spatially homogeneous (such as Bianchi type IX) solutions of the Einstein-Vlasov equations and investigate the large initial data case.

accepted.question_text: Prove the nonlinear stability of the Kerr black hole solution of general relativity.

evidence.quote: Problem P5: Prove the stability of the Kerr black hole.

accepted.question_text: Determine when a four-dimensional spacetime can be reconstructed explicitly from its scalar curvature invariants, and determine a minimal set of invariants sufficient for that characterization.

evidence.quote: Problem PF1 : Determine when a 4D spacetime can be explicitly constructed from its scalar curvature invariants and determine the minimal set of such invariants.

accepted.question_text: Formulate an appropriate mathematical definition of a dynamical horizon for an evolving black hole spacetime.

evidence.quote: Problem P6: Formulate an appropriate definition of a dynamical horizon.

accepted.question_text: Give a rigorous proof that test particles of negligible mass move on spacetime geodesics in general relativity.

evidence.quote: Problem P7 : Prove that test particles move on spacetime geodesics.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, in which a weakly turbulent cascade transfers energy to high frequencies and leads to black-hole formation, behaves differently in models more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse.

evidence.quote: Problem P8: Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability in Anti-de Sitter spacetime, which leads to a weakly turbulent mechanism that develops a cascade towards high frequencies leading to black hole formation, behaves differently in more general models than spherically symmetric scalar field collapse.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether higher-dimensional asymptotically flat black holes are unique under appropriate hypotheses.

evidence.quote: Problem P9: Determine the uniqueness of black holes in higher dimensions.

accepted.question_text: Determine the stability properties of higher-dimensional black holes.

evidence.quote: Problem P10: Determine the stability of higher dimensional black holes.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether singularity-resolution results proved in spatially homogeneous loop quantum gravity or loop quantum cosmology models can be extended to substantially more general settings.

evidence.quote: Problem P11: Can the singularity resolution results obtained in the spatially homogeneous spacetimes in LQG be proven in a more general setting.

accepted.question_text: Prove a cosmic no-hair theorem for generic inhomogeneous spacetimes, showing that sufficiently general expanding solutions with positive cosmological constant approach de Sitter-like behavior.

evidence.quote: Problem P12: Prove a cosmic no–hair theorem in generic inhomogeneous spacetimes.

accepted.question_text: Prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system is exactly the Mixmaster attractor, not merely a subset of it.

evidence.quote: Problem P13: Prove that the past attractor of the Bianchi type IX dynamical system coincides with the Mixmaster attractor ... rather than being a subset thereof.

accepted.question_text: Prove the Belinskii–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz locality conjecture in the fully general inhomogeneous setting.

evidence.quote: Problem P14: Prove the BKL locality conjecture in the general inhomogeneous context.

accepted.question_text: Prove that spikes occur in generic singularity formation and determine how such spikes affect any eventual proof about generic spacelike singularities.

evidence.quote: Problem P15: Prove the existence of spikes and determine their effect on any eventual generic singularity proofs.

accepted.question_text: Determine the structural stability of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities when general matter fields present in the early universe are included.

evidence.quote: Problem P16: Determine the structural stability of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities for general matter fields present in the early universe.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether isotropic singularities are typical in modified theories of gravity.

evidence.quote: Problem P17: Are isotropic singularities typical in modified theories of gravity.

accepted.question_text: Provide a rigorous mathematical definition of averaging in general relativity.

evidence.quote: Problem PF2 Provide a rigorous mathematical definition for averaging in GR.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether averaging can play an important role in cosmology and, in particular, what the largest coarse-graining scale is for matter and geometry that obey Einstein’s equations on smaller scales while the averaged evolution still satisfies the Einstein equations exactly.

evidence.quote: Problem PF3 Can averaging play an important role in cosmology. In particular, what is the largest scale that we can coarse-grain matter and geometry that obeys Einstein’s equations on smaller scales such that the average evolution is still an exact solution of Einstein’s equations.

accepted.question_text: Resolve the black-hole information paradox.

evidence.quote: Problem MPF1: Resolve the black hole information paradox.

accepted.question_text: Explain the cosmological constant problem and the nature of dark energy in a mathematically consistent way.

evidence.quote: Problem MPF2: The cosmological constant problem and dark energy.

accepted.question_text: Formulate a fully consistent theory of quantum gravity.

evidence.quote: Problem MPF3: Formulate a fully consistent theory of QG.

accepted.question_text: Determine how generic inflation is for generic initial data within a specific physical realization of inflation.

evidence.quote: Problem CMP1: What is the generality of inflation for generic initial data.

accepted.question_text: Determine the gravitational-wave waveforms emitted by binary black-hole systems well enough to support optimal detection and parameter extraction.

evidence.quote: Problem CMP2: Determine the predictions of emitted waveforms for binary black hole systems for optimal detection and parameter extraction.

accepted.question_text: Understand critical phenomena in gravitational collapse in general relativity, especially beyond highly symmetric settings.

evidence.quote: Problem CMP3: Understand critical phenomena in gravitational collapse in GR.
